Prati — Rome, Italy

🟡 Local press research

Average day Relatively safer night

In detail

Prati is an elegant, largely residential and institutional district next to the Vatican, known for wide boulevards, upscale shopping on Via Cola di Rienzo, and government offices. It is traditionally seen as one of Rome's safer central areas, and no reports of street violence or muggings turned up. However, multiple local outlets in mid-2026 reported a wave of burglaries - thieves breaking into basement storage rooms (cantine) and apartments, in one case prying open a door with a plastic sheet on Viale Giulio Cesare, in another using tattoo-linked suspects tied to an alleged Russian mafia connection. These are opportunistic daytime break-ins rather than a threat to pedestrians, so evenings and nights remain calm.
